articles.summary: Trial designed to improve outcomes through Signatera™-guided Treatment on MRD (TOMR), identifying high-risk patients for curative-intent treatment Natera, Inc. (Nasdaq:NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today announced that it has entered into a clinical collaboration agreement with Incyte (Nasdaq:INCY) for a new phase II study in colorectal cancer (CRC). The trial will evaluate INCA33890, Incyte’s investigational bispecific immunotherapy, in patients with stage 2/3 CRC who have completed surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT), incorporating Signatera as both a primary and secondary endpoint. Following ACT, patients will undergo longitudinal testing with Signatera for up to 12 months, and those who test Signatera MRD-positive and have no evidence of radiographic disease may be eligible for enrollment and treatment in the study. articles.summary: Supports serial testing in the surveillance setting for patients with early-stage HCC Natera, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today announced that its Signatera molecular residual disease (MRD) test has received Medicare coverage through the Centers for Medicare Medicaid Services’ (CMS) Molecular Diagnostics Services Program (MolDX) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The coverage includes serial Signatera testing in the surveillance setting for patients with early-stage HCC who have no post-surgical evidence of disease. More than 42,000 new cases of liver cancer are expected in the U.S. in 2026 1 and HCC accounts for approximately 90% of primary liver cancers. 2 Even after curative-intent treatment (e.g., surgery), patients face a high risk of recurrence that makes post-treatment monitoring critical. 2 This Medicare coverage decision was supported by a real-world study of 125 patients with HCC published in JCO Precision Oncology . articles.summary: Natera, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today announced a new collaboration with KSQ Therapeutics, Inc. (KSQ), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing cancer and autoimmune therapies based on precision functional genomics. The collaboration will incorporate Signatera™ Genome with Phased and Structural variants into an ongoing phase I/II clinical study of KSQ-004EX, an investigational engineered autologous tumor infiltrating lymphocyte (eTIL) therapy in which the genes encoding SOCS1 and Regnase-1 are inactivated using CRISPR/Cas9. In KSQ-004EX, a patient’s own tumor-fighting immune cells are genetically modified with the goal of enhancing their potency and durability against cancer. The phase I/II study (NCT06598371) is designed to evaluate patients with late-stage metastatic melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, colorectal cancer, pancreatic cancer, and cervical cancer. (NASDAQ: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today announced it will present important new Signatera data at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC) Annual Meeting, taking place November 4–8 in Phoenix, Arizona.
